Contextualizing Mathematical Problem-Solving Instruction for Secondary Students with Extensive Support Needs: A Systematic Replication
Jenny R. Root, Sarah K. Cox, Kat Davis, Nanette Hammons

Abstract
Replication research provides evidence to establish, refute, or support evidence-based practices. Systematic replications are also necessary to determine “what works for whom when.” The purpose of this study was to conduct a conceptual systematic replication to evaluate the effectiveness of a multicomponent treatment package on multiplicative problem solving for middle school students with extensive support needs. decisions.reason: Prior adjudication and state files are absent; the prior expert review returned undeterminable before reference and original-source recovery. The current source (d9c995e66c82eb9a.txt) remains abstract-only plus 31 deposited references. The abstract describes a conceptual systematic replication evaluating a multicomponent package—modified schema-based instruction (MSBI), contextualized percent-of-change word problems, a next-dollar purchasing strategy, and goal-setting with self-graphing—across three middle school students in a multiple-probe design, finding a functional relation and generalization to coupons and receipts. Under the codebook's description rule, this compound package and finding uniquely bind among the 31 references to e_1_3_3_19_1 (Root, Cox, Hammons, Saunders, & Gilley, 2018, 10.1352/1934-9556-56.6.442), whose verified primary abstract (01_root_metadata.body) evaluates MSBI, video anchors, and goal-setting with self-graphing on percent-of-change coupon and sufficiency problems for three secondary students with IDD and reports a functional relation with generalization to coupons, receipts, and menus. Competing references—Root et al. (2017, e_1_3_3_21_1, addition/subtraction personal finance), Browder et al. (2018, e_1_3_3_3_1, addition/subtraction word problems in dyads), Root et al. (2017, e_1_3_3_20_1, guide), Saunders et al. (2018, e_1_3_3_23_1, video prompting), and Spooner et al. (2019, e_1_3_3_26_1, review)—do not report this compound multiplicative percent-of-change and self-graphing intervention. Because e_1_3_3_19_1 is already shipped row 133, target_index 0 is not a missing row (shipped_right), while preserving that the current text is abstract-only with no in-text citation or requested outcome.
